locator.text: Display 31.8, p. 31, in the proof of Lemma 4.5

evidence: paper: c \ge c_K, \qquad G \ge \gamma_K, \qquad v \le B_K, \qquad cv \le B_K \quad \text{on } K.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The two lower bounds are stated, the two upper bounds are not. Lean's `compact_normalized_cone` conclusion gives one constant ε > 0 with ε ≤ c x and ε ≤ 2 * c x ^ 2 - (v x - 2) * j x ^ 2 on K; with the paper's G := 2c² − (v−2)j² and ε = min(c_K, γ_K) that is exactly `c ≥ c_K` and `G ≥ γ_K` (merging two constants into one is a routine weakening in the direction the proof uses). The paper's upper bounds `v ≤ B_K`, `cv ≤ B_K` and the normalization `B_K ≥ 1` were not found as a statement or a proof step anywhere I searched: in their place UniformCone.lean:86 takes `B` to be an upper bound of the image under the explicit threshold function x ↦ max 0 (max (2/c x) (max (v x / c x) (4 * c x * v x / d x))), so the upper bounds on v and cv are never formed separately. Both devices are the same appeal to compactness and both deliver one threshold valid on all of K (`compact_large_lag`, SeedConePaper.lean:48, which is the paper's second assertion).
